correctness.rationale: The lattice has index q^(2d-1), by taking the quotient of (Z/q²)^d by its diagonal order-q subgroup. A nonzero lattice vector divisible coordinatewise by q² has l1 length at least q²; in a nonzero diagonal residue every coordinate has absolute value at least q, so length is at least dq>q². Thus no edge degeneracies or triangles occur and every simple 4-cycle lifts to a coordinate square. The square-filled graph is the cubical torus's two-skeleton, with fundamental group the deck lattice and quotient map given by displacement. Subsequent attachments quotient this abelian group by the subgroup generated by the attached cycles' displacements. Straight coordinate walks give simple length-q² cycles (proper subwalks have shorter norm); they generate q²Z^d. The monotone length-dq walk to q1 is simple in the quotient since two different partial sums can differ by a lattice vector in [0,q]^d only if they are the two endpoints. It kills the remaining order-q class at dq. The lower bounds preclude earlier transitions. For q=3,d=4, V=2187, E=8748, and E−V+1=6562. Abelianization and tensoring with F_2 leave rank four at the square stage and zero from length nine onward, giving 6558 and 4 deaths at four and nine, respectively.
residual_risks: The finite recorded output checks the q=3,d=4 witness; the universal cutoff and group-map claims rely on the lift and norm arguments above.

checked_sources: Rajković arXiv:2611.09967v1, mod-two summary and limitations
value.rationale: This is a concrete, tunable witness against using a vanishing mod-two cycle summary to certify triviality. For each odd q≥3 it realizes a surviving group Z/q after all mod-two classes have disappeared, and changing d changes the interval length dq−q² without changing that surviving group. The explicit maps and simple-cycle threshold witnesses give more than the abstract observation that tensoring kills odd torsion.
residual_risks: The witness concerns the stated family and invariant; it neither characterizes all mod-two invisible groups nor implies practical detection limits outside this filtration.
